newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA LEV ENDS DOWN ON DLR BIDS FROM IMPORTERS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA LEV ENDS DOWN ON DLR BIDS FROM IMPORTERS.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at around
1,605-1,625 per dollar in light interbank volumes, down from
the morning's 1,580-1,595 due to increased foreign currency
buying from importers, dealers said.
"(Foreign currency) bidding from fuel and energy importers
pressured the lev. Trade however was thin," a bank dealer said.
The central bank was not spotted countering the lev fall.
Dollar supply from banks and clients was higher compared to
Monday as traders expected the lev to trade stable in the
broader range of 1,550-1,700 per dollar by the week's end with
the central bank preventing sharp shifts in the exchange rate.
Central bank officials were not immediately available for
comment.
Central bank governor Lyubomir Filipov said on Monday that
the bank was now strong enough to counter speculation against
the lev and support it near the current levels.
Interim prime minister Stefan Sofianski said that central
bank foreign exchange reserves have risen to $1.25 billion at
mid-May from $1.146 billion at end-April.
-- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
